questions.q: Where do custom Lightning web components appear in the Lightning App Builder?
options: They cannot be used in Lightning App Builder at all
Only inside Object Manager
In the Components panel, alongside standard components, often in a Custom section
Only on the Salesforce mobile app, never on desktop
questions.explain: Custom components show up in the same Components panel as standard ones, typically grouped under a Custom section.

questions.q: Who writes a custom Lightning web component?
options: The Platform App Builder, using only drag-and-drop
Salesforce support, on request
It is auto-generated by Lightning App Builder
A developer — the App Builder drags the finished component onto the canvas
questions.explain: A developer writes the component itself; the Platform App Builder places and configures it, but doesn't write its code.

questions.q: What is an 'exposed property' on a custom component?
options: A security vulnerability in the component
A developer-defined setting (like which list or filter) that an App Builder can configure without code
A field that is always required
A type of Apex trigger
questions.explain: Exposed properties are the configurable settings a developer deliberately built in, which the App Builder sets in the Page properties panel.

questions.q: What happens when the same custom component is previewed on the Salesforce mobile layout in App Builder?
options: It renders using its own responsive behavior — no separate mobile build is required by the App Builder
It must be entirely rebuilt as a separate mobile-only component
Custom components are never supported on mobile
It automatically becomes a Global Action
questions.explain: The App Builder canvas previews desktop and mobile without a separate build; responsiveness is handled in the component's own code.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the clean division of labor between Platform App Builder and developer?
options: The App Builder writes the component code; the developer only tests it
There is no distinction — both roles are identical
The developer configures page layouts; the App Builder writes Apex
The App Builder decides WHERE a component goes and configures its exposed properties; the developer decides WHAT the component can do
questions.explain: The App Builder places/configures components (the 'where'); the developer builds their capability (the 'what'). Neither role replaces the other.
